newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER SHOWS SUPERIORITY IN THE RAIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER SHOWS SUPERIORITY IN THE RAIN.

text.p: World championship leader Michael Schumacher of Germany demonstrated his and Ferrari's superiority in wet conditions again on Friday as they topped the times in opening practice for Sunday's French Grand Prix.

The 28-year-old double world champion clocked a best time of one minute 18.339 seconds, 1.4 seconds better than Italian Giancarlo Fisichella's best effort in his Jordan as the track dried out in the closing minutes.
But Schumacher said his success meant little.
"In the sort of track conditions we had today, we are very competitive and better than in the dry.
"If it does not rain on Sunday, we will have a very difficult race and I would prefer to have the same weather conditions for qualifying and the race as we had today.

"On my last run, I tried a new front wing which has looked promising in the wind tunnel. However, in today's rapidly changing codintions it is difficult to judge if it brought any improvement at all."

Fisichella was happier. "This session showed we have a good set-up for both wet and dry conditions. This is not the qualifying session so we will have to wait and see for tomorrow. But I must say I feel very confident at the moment."

Schumacher's Ferrari team mate Eddie Irvine of Britain, whose future is under threat from the Italian team's admiration for Finn Mika Salo of Tyrrell, was not given a chance to go out on slicks and wound up in 20th place out of the 22 runners.

Irvine's contract expires at the end of the year and Ferrari's option to renew it expires at the end of July. Their inactivity - despite Schumacher's forthright support for Irvine - has suggested they are considering approaching Salo to succeed the Northern Ireland man next season.
Canadian Jacques Villeneuve finished fifth in the session.
Italian Jarno Trulli, replacing the injured Olivier Panis in the Prost team, was 19th fastest.
Frenchman Panis suffered double fractures to both legs when he crashed during the Canadian Grand Prix two weeks ago.

Tarso Marques, the 21-year-old Brazilian who was called up to replace Trulli at Minardi was 14th fastest while Norberto Fontana of Argentina who replaced broken arm victim Italian Gianni Morbidelli at Sauber, wound up 18th on his debut.
